data: Phase 9: volatility-managed rule on 15 international country funds (out-of-sample)

Rules were committed to git before any international data was downloaded. Same rule as Phase 5: weight = min(1, typical vol / forecast vol), no leverage, one-day delay, 10 bps per unit of turnover, rest in T-bills. Benchmark: buy & hold the same fund. Evaluation from 2002-03-05 (earliest, after the 500-day warm-up; later for funds with a later data start) to 2026-11-09. PASS = smaller max drawdown AND Sharpe difference >= 0.
Average Sharpe difference by region (same-date block bootstrap)
Max drawdown inside crisis windows, averaged over funds with data

Reading it (as of the first run): under the pre-registered rule the verdict is CRASH INSURANCE ONLY. Managed exposure cut the maximum drawdown in all 14 funds and in every fund in 2008-09 and 2020 (11 of 14 in 2022), but it did not raise Sharpe: 3 of 14 passed, and the pooled Sharpe difference is about zero. SPY (in-sample) looked better than any foreign fund, so the US Sharpe gain was probably partly luck.

Disclosures: (1) the project's data loader starts Yahoo data in 2000, not 1996, so after the 500-day warm-up evaluation starts in 2002 at the earliest and the 2000-02 crash is mostly missed. (2) Belgium (EWK) had 371 zero-range days; the start-date rule left too little data, so it is excluded and 14 funds are counted. (3) A post-hoc check (not part of the rules): with 0 bps costs the pooled Sharpe difference is still only +0.005, so costs are not the reason. Turnover averages about 5.5x a year.
